Headline: Traffic restrictions ahead of the Asian Games to impact in-land freight movement
Details:
From August 18 to September 2, Indonesia will host the 18th Asian Games, a pan-Asian multi-sport event which will be held in Jakarta and Palembang. The opening and closing ceremonies will be held in Jakarta and reports suggest that the sporting event will draw around 17,000 athletes and sports officials as well as more than 100,000 international spectators. The tournament will include a variety of 42 games, out of which 20 will be held inside the Gelora Bung Karno sports complex in Jakarta and the rest will be spread across Jakarta Convention Centre, the International Expo, Ancol Beach and other locations in the North, East, and South of Jakarta. In Palembang, most sporting events will take place at the Jakabaring Sport City and Bumi Sriwijaya Stadium.

To cater to this large sporting event, authorities have increased flights at Soekarno Hatta International Airport (CGK) and Sultan Mahmud Badaruddin II International Airport (PLM) which serves Jakarta and Palembang respectively. Furthermore, environmental cleanup programs, as well as traffic restrictions, have been imposed in Jakarta to curb air pollution and reduce congestion. An odd-even license plate policy on vehicles has been on a trial run since July 2 to measure the athletes’ average travel time during the events. The regulation stipulates that vehicles with license plates ending in odd numbers will only be allowed to travel in certain zones on odd-numbered dates. The same applies to plates ending with even numbers on even-numbered dates. The trial period ended on July 31 and the official implementation of the policy came into effect on August 1 again. This will last until September 2 with the hours extended from 06:00 to 21:00 (local time). The notice issued by the transportation authorities indicated that the policy also applies to cargo trucks as they fall under the category of Group III, IV and V vehicles, which includes containers and trailers.

While the games will not have a significant impact on ocean and airfreight as well as on customs clearance processes, in-land freight movement including pickup and delivery services are likely to face localized disruptions due to the scheduled operating hours of a few toll gates in Jakarta during the games. From August 18 to September 2, authorities will reportedly restrict the operating hours of the following toll gates:
  
Toll gates closed between 06:00 to 17:00 (local time):
•	Pintu Tol Angke 2
•	Pintu Tol Tanjung Duren
•	Pintu Tol Slipi 2
•	Pintu Tol Taman Mini 1 

Toll gates closed between 12:00 to 21:00 (local time):
•	Pintu Tol Angke 1
•	Pintu Tol Slipi 1
•	Pintu Tol Taman Mini 2

Trucks carrying goods can use the Kebon Bawang toll gate between 22:00 to 05:00 to access the Tanjung Priok Port to the Inner Circle toll road. Furthermore, reports indicate that trucking will be diverted through the arterial road and will be allowed to enter through the Rorotan Toll Gate and Cakung directly to the Outer Ring Road. 

According to sources, around 60,000 security personnel will be deployed during the Asian Games to ensure public security which may result in vehicle spot checks for trucks that are operating at night due to the change in schedules. Customers with interests in shipments to Indonesia during the Asian Games should keep in mind the traffic policy changes and the potential delays in in-land freight movement. Customers are advised to liaise with local partners to keep abreast of local traffic regulations to ensure timely cargo and pickup delivery services.
Category: Roadway Closure / Disruption, Ground Transportation Advisory, Cargo Disruption

Headline: UPDATE - Hong Kong: Polytechnic University operation ends; demonstrations planned for this weekend in Hong Kong
Details: Social media sources indicate that demonstrations are planned for this weekend in Hong Kong. The planned protests follow a week of relative peace following district council elections last Sunday, 24 November, which saw a majority victory by pro-democracy candidates. The call to demonstrate is due in part to Chief Executive Carrie Lam's acknowledgment of public dissatisfaction, but perceived unwillingness to make political concessions following the elections. Additionally, some protesters are believed to be motivated by the events at Hong Kong Polytechnic University, which saw 12 days of violence between demonstrators and riot police before authorities cleared the location. A major rally has been called for Sunday, 1 December, with a subsequent strike on 2 December which will reportedly target morning commutes. Clashes with police cannot be ruled out at these events.

Headline: Evaluations Continue Following Severe Winter Storm That Killed 13 in Mediterranean Spain and France
Details:
On Thursday, the death toll in Spain from a storm, locally referred to as Storm Gloria, rose to 13 with an additional four people missing. Mediterranean coastal areas of Spain, including Catalonia, Murcia, and Andalusia, and the Balearic Islands were hardest hit in Spain, with Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez surveying heavily impacted areas on Thursday ahead of a government emergency meeting on Friday as response measures are ongoing. The storm brought wind gusts in excess of 60 miles per hour along with heavy rain and strong waves. The majority of storm-related deaths occurred in Catalonia and Valencia. While the storm had moved from Spain, several rivers in the country s northeast burst their banks on Thursday and rice paddies in the Ebro River delta between Barcelona and Valencia were hard hit from a storm surge that extended about two miles inland. The storm also brought snow to the Pyrenees and flooding to lower-elevation areas of southern France, though no related fatalities in France are known. In France s Pyr n es-Orientales and Aude departments, as much as five months of rain has fallen within three days, prompting more than 1,500 evacuations.

Assessment: Prime Minister Sanchez said that climate change is  accentuating  storms such as Gloria, while forecasters in France noted that Gloria was the worst winter storm to strike the region since 1982. France and Spain experienced heavy flooding in October 2019, however, and both the intensity and frequency of such storms are generally believed to be hallmarks of climate change. Such storms are capable of disrupting regional transportation, damaging coastal infrastructure, and exacerbating erosion that can leave coastal areas more vulnerable to future severe weather events. In more mountainous regions, the heavy snowfall from storm systems typically heightens the risk of avalanches, and data from local officials regarding any restricted areas should be observed. While damage assessments and recovery efforts continue in both France and Spain, it is advised to continue monitoring river levels in affected areas for any further flood risk, to avoid any persisting areas of high water, including while driving, and to heed the guidance of local authorities.

Headline: Stevedore strike at Port of Santos to remain unresolved during Carnaval
Details:
Sindestiva (Sindicato dos Estivadores de Santos, Sao Vicente, Guaruja e Cubatao), the largest stevedore union representing dockworkers on the Sao Paulo coast, declared the commencement of a strike at the Port of Santos on March 1 at 7:00 (local time). The strike action is the latest to involve stevedores airing grievances against the port management at Brazil’s largest seaport, and the first of 2019. 
The warning for this strike was issued on February 19, after a Superior Labor Court decision on February 11 permitted the Port of Santos to employ contractors to quantities of up to 100% of its workforce, revoking an earlier agreement from 2015 that permitted only a maximum of 50% contractor employment at the port. The strike also provides the union the opportunity to air grievances over pay and benefits. After a union meeting on February 26, the strike was confirmed on February 28, and is in progress as of this writing. 
What complicates matters is that the strike coincides with the Carnaval holiday in Brazil. Brazilian supply chains and transportation thoroughfares, like many locales which commemorate the holiday, slow down and gradually resume production after Ash Wednesday. Manufacturers traditionally give employees time off for the Carnaval period, with typical holiday duration lasting for about 1 week, starting on the preceding Friday. In extreme cases, the holiday may even extend to 21 days. Sources state that the port management and Sindestiva representatives willing to meet and negotiate during the holiday is unlikely at best.
While past incidents impacting the Port of Santos have been relatively harmless, this open-ended strike over a longer period without any negotiation in sight poses greater uncertainty. Such uncertainty without a resolution is likely to cause cargo delays and subsequent backlogs. As such, those relying on the Port of Santos as a maritime hub are advised to monitor developments. While strikes of this nature typically make provisions for the unimpeded circulation of perishable and element-sensitive goods, no such provisions have been explicitly mentioned at present.

Headline: UPDATE 1 - Australia unlikely to directly retaliate against mainland China’s targeted measures; foreign policy position also unlikely to change
Details: According to Chinese and international media reports, Chinese traders have received an informal notice from authorities that Australian products in seven categories – barley, sugar, lobster, wine, timber, coal, and copper ore and concentrate – will not be cleared in customs from 6 November. The Chinese government has denied that there are any restrictions on Australian commodities, and the implementation of the notice has yet to be confirmed. Australian exporters have nevertheless already cancelled shipments to China and Chinese traders have cancelled orders.The timing and extent of Chinese action against Australian imports give credibility to recent media reporting that this reflects Chinese government policy and not just buyers’ commercial decisions. China-Australia relations have deteriorated significantly in recent months, particularly after the Australian government called for an independent inquiry into the origins of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) in April. Beginning in May, Chinese authorities imposed a series of restrictions on Australian imports, ostensibly due to alleged breaches of trade practices (resulting in tariffs on barley) or quality issues found during routine product inspections (affecting some shipments of beef, barley, lobster, and timber). On 9 October, there were reports that some Chinese ports had been told not to accept Australian coal. Although coal import quotas are not uncommon, this came days after a meeting between foreign ministers of the recently revived Quadrilateral Security Dialogue (Quad) nations, comprising Australia, India, Japan, and the United States. China has previously labelled the Quad as an “Asian NATO” (see Australia-India-Japan-US:2 October 2020: Future of Australia-India-Japan-US Quad dialogue and maritime security in the Indo-Pacific). Australian Trade Minister Simon Birmingham has accused China of taking “discriminatory action” against Australia in imposing import restrictions. China has repeatedly denied any targeting of Australia, stating that reduced imports were the result of buyers’ decisions.Given its vulnerability to wider Chinese discrimination against Australian imports, the Australian government is unlikely to retaliate. According to the Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade, China accounted for 32.6% (AUD153.2 billion, or USD111.1 billion) of its total goods and services exports in the financial year ending 2019. According to China’s National Bureau of Statistics, Australia in 2019 only accounted for 1.9% of mainland Chinese exports globally and 3.8% of mainland China’s exports to the Asia-Pacific and Oceania regions. This indicates that, while China has scope to extend restrictions on other Australian imports, Australia is unlikely to respond in reciprocal measures and equivalent degree. Rather, the Australian government will probably increase conciliatory advances towards China, notably through public statements on the importance of the bilateral relationship. The government is also likely to rein in backbenchers, both within the Liberal-National coalition and the Labor Party opposition, who frequently criticise China publicly. In addition, Australia will probably refrain from taking a prominent role in any further international initiatives challenging China, as it did in April when it led an international call for a COVID-19 inquiry. Repeated Chinese import restrictions are unlikely to result in Australian reversal on foreign policy issues challenged by China, however. Although Australia will avoid taking a prominent role in future international initiatives against China, its participation in the ongoing India-Japan-US Malabar naval exercise this month indicates that the Australian government is unlikely to reverse core policies that are at odds with China. This includes Australia’s commitment to the Quad grouping and its stance on issues such as Hong Kong SAR and the South China Sea. Participation in the current Malabar exercise contrasts with the last time Australia took part in 2007: China’s negative response resulted in the government of then-prime minister Kevin Rudd withdrawing from the exercises and accompanying security talks, resulting in the dissolution of the Quad. Nevertheless, given its economic vulnerability vis-à-vis China, Australia will probably seek to adjust its approach to the Quad and other regional defence activities by minimising its profile. Indicators of changing risk environmentIncreasing riskIf November and December 2020 shipments of Australian coal continue to show signs of regulatory targeting indicated by significant congestions in major ports in mainland China, this would further signal worsening bilateral relationships due to Beijing’s evident refusal to lift restrictions on Australian coal during the winter months – traditionally a period of higher power consumption and coal demand.If China imposes import restrictions or heightens regulatory barriers against Australian iron ore, this would indicate a significant worsening of bilateral relations. In 2019, 62% of China’s iron ore imports came from Australia. The economic cost of Chinese targeting of iron ore would likely be disproportionally borne in China’s infrastructure sector, which remains important in its investment-led economic recovery and relies on an inexpensive and stable supply of steel. Targeted measures against iron ore would indicate both a long-term policy shift of trade diversion from Australia to alternative markets for raw materials as well as intent to significantly damage the Australian economy, given that iron ore is Australia’s largest export to China.The passage into law of draft Australian federal legislation affecting foreign, particularly Chinese, commercial interests in Australia – likely in January 2021 (see Australia:8 June 2020: Proposed changes to Australia’s foreign investment rules likely to target Chinese investors, increasing risk of forced divestments and Australia:4 September 2020: Australia’s proposed legislation on agreements between states/territories and foreign governments indicates increased likelihood of state contract cancellation) – would be a further indicator of the trajectory of relations between Australia and China. Any amendments targeting Chinese interests more explicitly would probably result in a further deterioration of relations, increasing the likelihood of further restrictions on Australian goods and services or other targeted measures against Australian assets.Decreasing riskDirect talks between either Australian Prime Minister Scott Morrison and Chinese President Xi Jinping or their respective foreign ministers would increase the likelihood of an improvement in relations.Any delays or a government reversal on passing the draft legislation affecting Chinese interests would slightly decrease the likelihood of further Chinese restrictions on Australian products, as long as Australia avoids further high-profile diplomatic confrontations with China.© 2020, IHS Markit Inc. Headline: Philippines: Tropical Depression Samuel to bring heavy rain to Visayas and Mindanao areas
Details: PAGASA, the national weather bureau, has confirmed that heavy rain will impact Visayas and Mindanao areas from Monday evening as a tropical depression travels towards land. Samuel entered the Philippine Area of Responsibility on Sunday morning and is currently east southeast of Surigao del Sur, with sustained winds of 55kph. The storm has the potential to unleash floods and landslides in Caraga, Davao Oriental and Compostela Valley regions starting Monday. Outer rain bands of the current depression will impact Metro Manila. Travellers are advised to heed to any instructions from the authorities and exercise caution when travelling in adverse weather conditions.

Headline: ZIM to fine shippers for misdeclared hazardous cargoes
Details: Industry sources indicate on September 3 that Haifa-based ZIM Integrated Shipping Services announced its intent to implement a penalty of USD 12,000 (EUR 10,800) per container for misdeclared or undeclared hazardous cargoes, with a definitive fine quantity unknown as of reporting, and it is unknown when this penalty will come into effect. ZIM will hold the customer on record liable and responsible for costs and consequences related to violations, fines, damages, incidents, claims and corrective measures resulting from cases of shipment of such cargo. The move is similar to that implemented by other cargo shipping lines in the aftermath of the Yantian Express fire.

Headline: Truckers' demonstration impedes access to Port of Santos
Details: Local media sources indicate on December 10 that the truckers’ demonstration on the Presidente Dutra Highway (BR-116) is impeding road access to the Port of Santos in Sao Paulo. The demonstrations are occurring all over the BR-116 highway from the Vale do Paraiba, SP to the Zona da Mata, MG, in grievance against a recent Supreme Federal Tribunal decision regarding penalties for non-compliance with the minimum freight table. The possibility of escalations of these events is very likely due to the freight table legislation expiring by December 31. Those shipping to the Port of Santos should anticipate the possibility of further industrial action impeding port access and should develop contingencies accordingly.

Headline: Thailand: Flood warnings in place for 18 provinces due to Tropical Storm Kajiki
Details: According to Thai news reports, the Disaster Prevention and Mitigation Department (DPMD)  has placed 18 provinces on alert for possible flash floods, forest runoffs and landslides due to heavy rainfall from Tropical Storm Kajiki. The storm is currently over neighbouring Vietnam and its exact trajectory is not clear. Thunderstorms and downpours are expected in areas of 55 provinces, but the worst of the conditions is forecast to impact Mae Hong Son, Chiang Mai, Chiang Rai, Nan, Phrae, Uttaradit, Phichit, Tak, Phetchabun, Sukhothai, Phitsanulok, Loei, Khon Kaen, Chaiyaphum, Kanchanaburi, Ratchaburi, Ranong and Phang Nga. Meanwhile, 12 northern and northeastern provinces – Phrae, Phitsanulok, Uttaradit, Nan, Phetchabun, Udon Thani, Sakhon Nakhon, Kalasin, Roi Et, Yasothon and Ubon Ratchathani. In addition, the four eastern provinces of Chon Buri, Rayong, Chanthaburi and Trat, as well as six southern provinces of Ranong, Phang Nga, Phuket, Krabi, Trang and Satun are under strong wind/waves warnings; small boats have been prohibited from sailing during the next 1-2 days.

Headline: Boxship attacked by pirates in Gulf of Guinea
Details: Industry sources reported that perpetrators tried to board the boxship ""Kota Satria"" while the vessel was sailing in the Gulf of Guinea on February 21, 2019. More than four men armed with guns onboard an unlit fast boat attempted to board the vessel. Two of the perpetrators attempted to hook a ladder to ship’s hull. However, they were not successful and slowed down the pursuit. The perpetrators then fired two gunshots toward the ship’s bridge and subsequently to the ship’s accommodation. The master initiated security procedures and contacted the company security officer as well as the company’s armed escort vessel and the Nigerian Navy and carried out evasive maneuver. Consequently, the fast boat aborted the pursuit. There were no injuries to the ship’s crew and no damage to the vessel reported. In addition, no items were stolen. Following the incident, the ship met an armed escort ship and proceeded to the port of Onne where it berthed on February 22 and sailed on February 28, bound to Singapore, ETA March 27.

Headline: Annual maintenance schedule for Three Gorges Dam Lock System released
Details:
This week, the intended maintenance schedule for the Three Gorges Dam Lock System has been issued by the Chinese Ministry of Transport. The timelines for the maintenance works were said to be as follows:

-	Three Gorges South Line Ship Lock: The overhaul time of the Three Gorges Ship Lock in 2018 shall begin on February 19 from 08:00 AM and will last for 33 days.
-	Gezhou Dam No. 1 Ship Lock: The overhaul time of the Gezhou Dam No. 1 Lock in 2018 shall begin on February 26 from 08:00 AM and will last for 20 days.

Please note that the approximate average waiting time to pass through the Dam was 15 days during the Three Gorges’ North Ship lock maintenance in 2017, which impacted the transit time to upper Yangtze River areas. Therefore, this maintenance will impact cargo transshipped via Shanghai. In addition, as of December 2017, barge companies, including COSCO, reportedly delayed space confirmation by at least one week due to extreme congestion at the Three Gorges Dam, and imposed a congestion surcharge to cover increasing local costs. Transit times to Shanghai were on average taking 10 days longer. Customers are advised to consider alternative transport modes, including a rail service from Chongqing to Qinzhou for westbound shipments to India and Southeast Asia.

Headline: New COVID-19 measures at Port of  Tanjung Priok

1.	Every crew member who will start their task on a ship is required to validate the RDT (Rapid Diagnostic Test) or PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) certificate before joining the ship, minimum 1 day before the ship’s departure. This is to avoid close contact with the crew on the ship if the result is reactive/positive.

2.	If the RDT result is reactive, crew member must do the PCR test, not join the ship and self-isolate for 14 days, or until the PCR result is negative.

3.	If the PCR result is positive, crew member must be treated with the help of the Covid19 Handling Task Force.

4.	If the crew member is already on the ship and just checked the RDT, and the result is reactive, there will be a PCR test for all crew members who have contact, and the ship will be disinfected. Before the PCR result is issued, the ship will be quarantined.

c. If you have a fever, cough, shortness of breath, contact the health officer immediately.

Headline: CMA CGM Hit by Ransomware Attack; Cyberattacks on the Rise in the Logistics Industry
Details:
Over the weekend of Saturday, September 27, and Sunday, September 28, the French shipping container liner company CMA CGM was targeted by a ransomware cyberattack. CMA CGM’s website and the websites of some of its subsidiaries were unavailable, except for the group’s corporate website. While initially the company stated that the issues were caused by problems with internal IT infrastructure, the situation was confirmed to be due to a cyberattack through a message on the corporate website’s homepage, as well as through a social media post by the Vice President, Joel Gentil. The Ceva Logistics subsidiary was reportedly unaffected, and the CMA CGM network remained mostly available to customers for booking and operations requests. Booking and operations services were disrupted at several Chinese offices, including Shanghai, Shenzhen, and Guangzhou. Hackers used Ragnar Locker data encryption ransomware in the attack, but external access to CMA CGM applications was purportedly interrupted when the breach was detected, preventing the malware from spreading. The full extent of the breach remains unclear. On Sunday, September 28, the hackers responsible allegedly contacted CMA CGM via email demanding to be contacted through live chat within two days to pay for a decryption key; however the price has not been disclosed. An investigation into how CMA CGM systems became infected is underway.



Assessment: CMA CGM is the world’s fourth-largest shipping container liner. The top three largest shipping liners have all been victims of cyberattacks in recent years, with Maersk in 2017, Cosco in 2018, and Mediterranean Shipping Co in 2020. The 2017 Maersk attack was reportedly collateral damage of the NotPetya cyberattack concentrated on Ukraine, and resulted in 12 days of disrupted activities and approximately $300 million in losses for the company. Logistics companies have purportedly been increasingly targeted in cyberattacks, with multimodal and automotive logistics company GEFCO suffering a breach on September 20 this year. Increased digitization of shipping and port operations are likely to contribute to increased vulnerability of the industry to cyberattacks in the future. It is advised to monitor developments associated with the investigation into the CMA CGM attack, as well as new information regarding the extent of the breach. It is also advised to monitor industry trends related to digitization and cybersecurity measures adopted by corporations in the sector as means of safeguarding internal infrastructure against future attacks.
Category: Public Safety / Security, Network Disruption, Maritime Advisory

Headline: Search Efforts Continue After Ship Capsized Off Japan; Cattle Exports from New Zealand Suspended
Details:
Japanese authorities reported on Thursday that a cargo ship, the Gulf Livestock 1, had capsized in the East China Sea, about 115 miles west of Kagoshima Prefecture’s Amami Oshima. The ship sent a distress signal early Wednesday morning local time while in the area of Typhoon Maysak. A single crew member was rescued by the Japan Coast Guard on Wednesday night. As of this writing, no further sign of the ship or wreckage has been discovered.



Assessment: The Gulf Livestock 1 was transporting nearly 6,000 cattle from Napier, New Zealand, to the Port of Jingtang in Tangshan, China. According to the crew member who was rescued, a Filipino national, the ship suffered engine trouble before capsizing under high waves. An additional 42 crew members remain missing, including 38 Filipinos, two Australians, and two New Zealanders. Search and rescue efforts were initially delayed by the ongoing typhoon, but Japanese authorities report that weather has now cleared and operations are continuing. The Gulf Livestock 1 was a 450-foot cargo ship, constructed in 2002 and weighing 11,947 tons. The ship was registered in Panama. Officials in New Zealand have temporarily suspended cattle exports as an investigation into the ship’s situation is conducted.

Headline: Additional Shipping Delays Possible Amid Ongoing Dispute Between Patrick Terminals and Dockworkers
Details:
On Wednesday, an ongoing dispute between dockworkers with the Maritime Union of Australia (MUA) and Patrick Terminals will be brought before the Fair Work Commission. The dispute, centering on pay and working conditions, has led to some delays to shipping, particularly at Sydney’s Port Botany. While the union has acknowledged an overtime ban is in place, it has denied any other industrial action has been carried out recently. One-day strikes that had been planned at Port Botany and Brisbane for this coming Friday have been canceled. Media sources reported on Wednesday morning local time that the MUA had offered to keep current working arrangements with Patrick for the next year in exchange for a 2.5 percent raise for workers.



Assessment: The MUA ended a similar dispute with DP World last Friday, while a resolution with Hutchison Ports is expected soon. According to Patrick, the MUA’s overtime ban has cost it 31 percent of its crane teams at ports across Australia, with Port Botany even more affected. The company has stated that as many as 40 ships and up to 90,000 containers have been delayed from unloading, including medical supplies. The union has denied this, instead saying that there have been only minor delays, which it has attributed to the company canceling several recent night shifts. It is not immediately clear whether the offer made by the MUA on Wednesday will resolve the dispute. It is advised to follow developments should disruptions and delays to shipping continue from the labor dispute or in case of further strike actions.

Headline: UPDATE 1 - Chennai lockdown until end of June after surge in COVID-19 cases to have cargo implications
Details: Updated sources reported that the Tamil Nadu-imposed lockdown from June 19 to June 30 after COVID-19 cases surged will have cargo disruption implications. According to the Tamil Nadu government, a full lockdown will commence for Chennai, Thiruvallur, Chengalpet & Kanchipuram districts until the end of June. However, shops selling essential items and restaurants will be allowed to remain open from early morning until 14.00 local time during the lockdown. Airports, seaports, and ground cargo transportation in Chennai will only be allowed to handle essential commodities, to include food, pharmaceuticals, petroleum, derivative products of the aforementioned, security, medical, financials, IT, and telecommunications. Furthermore, shippers/consignees may need to produce declarations confirming ability of facilities to handle cargo, and inbound cargo can proceed as long as the shipper and consignee are aligned for movement. Furthermore, only 33% of customs officers are allowed to operate in Chennai's air & sea ports, so a noticeable customs operational impact is anticipated.

Headline: Eastern China   Cleanup operations continue after flooding impacted the area. Incident closed.
Details:
Media sources reported that heavy rainfall from the remnants of Tropical Storm Rumbia caused flooding in the eastern provinces of Shandong, Liaoning, Jiangsu, Anhui, and Henan. Flooding was reported in Quanzhou City. At least 32 people were killed since Rumbia made landfall including 14 people killed in Shandong and 12 people killed in Anhui. At least 15 people were missing. One police officer participating in rescue operations was killed in Shouguang and one other police officer went missing. More than 10,000 firefighters were deployed to Shouguang due to the flooding. 

Approximately 140,000 people were displaced, including 102,800 in Shandong Province and 37,800 in Liaoning Province. More than 34,400 homes were damaged, an estimated 110,000 greenhouse farms were damaged, and almost 820,000 acres of cropland was destroyed. The damage to crops in Shouguang caused Shandong to raise produce prices. Flooding reportedly caused economic losses of US$ 1.45 billion in Shandong. Residual disruptions may persist as cleanup operations continue. This incident is closed.

Headline: Alleged Houthi Attack on Oil Tanker in Red Sea Highlights Threat to Maritime Security
Details:
Saudi Arabian officials confirmed that a mine exploded off the coast of Shuqaiq, Saudi Arabia, and damaged a Maltese-flagged oil tanker on Wednesday, November 25. Reportedly, the MT Agrari tanker, managed by a Greek private company, was struck approximately three feet above the waterline, which caused an explosion and subsequent fire in the Red Sea, near the Shuqaiq Steam Power Plant. Following the attack, Saudi Arabia claimed to successfully intercept and destroy the explosive-laden boat that perpetrated the attack. There were no immediate reports of any hazardous contents spilling into the water and no reports of any injuries. Headline: Truckers' union announces strike in Sao Paulo state
Details: Local media sources indicate on November 28 that truckers organized by Sindicam Ourinhos have announced their intention to strike on November 29. The truckers, mostly in agricultural commodity shipping, have announced their grievance at lack of adherence by major firms such as Cutrale, Louis Dreyfus, and CitroSuco to the minimum freight table signed into law in August as part of a deal to end the May truckers’ strike. The table is due to expire on December 31, at the end of President Michel Temer’s term and the beginning of that of Jair Bolsonaro, a topic raised by truckers after an October 29 wildcat strike and discussions by the CNT truckers’ union of renewing strike activity nationally. A strike also has the possibility of mobilizing Sindicam Santos, involving blocked highways and impeding shipments to and from Brazil’s principal seaport of entry. Those shipping in Sao Paulo should anticipate a scenario similar to that of May 21 through 31 and should plan accordingly.

Cosatu and Saftu have stated that they intend to cause as much disruption as possible through these demonstrations.

Widespread flooding has been reported, as the Philippines remains inundated from a series of typhoons over October and November. The greater Manila area was heavily impacted. This event is closed.

Headline: Severe Storms Thursday Night Lead to at Least One Death, SOE for 11 Counties in Upstate NY
Details:
On Friday, November 1, Governor Andrew Cuomo declared a state of emergency (SOE) for 11 counties in Upstate New York following widespread severe weather on Thursday night. The storms brought heavy rainfall and high winds which caused flooding and damage across the region. At least one death in Herkimer County was blamed on the flooding. An unknown number of structures across the region suffered damage in the storm, mainly from downed trees and debris caused by the high winds. Areas along the banks of Lake Erie saw significant flooding with Buffalo reporting a seven-foot rise in water levels in just several hours. Widespread power outages and numerous road closures were also reported across the region. There were no reports of widespread evacuations in relation to the storms and subsequent flooding. The state of emergency declaration included the following counties: Cayuga, Chautauqua, Dutchess, Erie, Essex, Hamilton, Herkimer, Montgomery, Oneida, Saratoga, and Warren. 

Assessment: The state of emergency declaration activated the State Emergency Operations Center to help with recovery and rebuilding efforts. In addition, at least 200 members of the state National Guard were activated to assist with cleanup and response operations. The high winds from the storm, upwards of 60 miles per hour for some areas, caused power outages to at least 241,000 utility customers at the storm's peak. As of this writing, the majority of customers have had power restored. At least 60 road closures were reported across the region, though these were mostly local roads and not major highways. An unknown number of roads suffered significant damage and will take multiple days or weeks to be repaired. Flooding has largely receded; however, rain has been forecast beginning Monday night. As of this writing, a Flood Warning remains in effect for Warren County until Wednesday, November 6 at 10:00 AM EST. Customers are advised to use caution in affected due to storm debris and the possibility of damaged roads. Heed all instructions from local authorities.

Headline: Nationwide Juneteenth Actions Planned in Relation to Ongoing Use of Force Protests
Details:
Widespread protest activity is expected across the United States in relation to the upcoming Juneteenth holiday on Friday, June 19. Juneteenth commemorates the full emancipation of slaves in 1865. Generally, the holiday is celebrated with parades and celebrations; however, with ongoing use-of-force protests across the United States, many activists are using the holiday for additional protests both about police use of force, as well as racial inequality. Major actions are planned in a number of cities including Tulsa, OK; Washington, DC: Los Angeles, CA; New York, NY; Seattle, WA; and Chicago, IL, among others. In addition to the expected protest activity, dockworkers with the International Longshore and Warehouse Union (ILWU) have planned a solidarity strike for Friday at 29 ports along the West Coast. 



Assessment: While widespread protests are likely in relation to Juneteenth, these protests are expected to have a more celebratory tone than what has occurred during use-of-force protests over the last three weeks. Many of the planned actions on Friday have been described as “block party” type events with performances like singing and dancing, rather than just protest marches. However, marches are likely to still occur and several localities, including Washington DC, have called for Juneteenth protests with intentions to block major roads and interstates. The protest action planned in Tulsa also presents a chance for escalation due to a planned rally by President Trump in the city on Saturday. The rally had been initially scheduled to be held on Friday but was pushed back following widespread public outcry. As such, the tensions at the Tulsa action are likely to be heightened and could potentially lead to clashes. Road closures are likely to be the main disruption from the Juneteenth actions; however, escalation of protest activity cannot be ruled out. The public is advised to anticipate associated disruptions and avoid protest activity due to the potential for incidental violence, such as unruly crowd behavior and/or the use of crowd control measures by law enforcement.

Headline: UPDATE 2 - Police and military operation ends with seven stowaways in custody near Shanklin, Isle of Wight
Details: It is being reported that seven stowaways have been arrested following a police and military operation on an oil tanker near Shanklin on the Isle of Wight today (25 October). The Special Boat Service were deployed to the scene after the stowaways became violent to the ship's crew. The ship was travelling from Lagos in Nigeria to Southampton in England, when the Liberian-flagged oil tanker dropped its anchor and the crew retreated to the citadel, which is a secure area in which they can lock themselves into, making it nearly impossible for others to get in. From the citadel, the crew were able to communicate with the Maritime Coastguard Agency. A three nautical mile exclusion zone is still in place around the vessel and it is unknown when it when be lifted.

Headline: UPDATE: Congestion issues ameliorate slightly at Los Angeles and Long Beach
Details: Shipping sources indicate on January 30 that congestion conditions are showing signs of improvement at the Port of Los Angeles and Long Beach. While congestion times average 3.31 days, higher than the 2.5-3 day 2018 average, it is an improvement over the 7.5-day peak in late 2018. The extent of the congestion has been described as reaching inland ports in Southern California as well. The congestion is due to increased volumes passing through the port as well as reduced productivity during the holiday season. Some shipping lines have diverted calls to the Port of Long Beach instead or may even omit the port call and discharge containers at the Port of Oakland. The cause has been attributed to the import surge of December 2018 that left a glut of containers with few chassis's available to meet the demand. Landside congestion with long lines of trucks at the terminal gates has also been reported, likely resulting in higher costs for end customers. Customers should expect the situation to continue until at least the beginning of February 2019.

Headline: Brief Seizure of Tanker near Strait of Hormuz Reflects Persistent Risk of Maritime Incidents
Details:
On Wednesday, media sources indicated that the brief seizure of a Hong Kong-flagged oil tanker in the Gulf of Oman, near the Strait of Hormuz, on April 14 may have been a botched operation by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC). According to reports, armed men boarded and commandeered the Hong Kong-flagged SC Taipei, bound for Saudi Arabia, near Iran’s Ras al-Kuh coast. The ship was detained for a short time before it and its 22-member crew of Chinese nationals were released and underway under the captain’s control. A United Nations database reportedly listed the mail-forwarding address for the ship’s owners as associated with the Shanghai-based Aoxing Ship Management, which was sanctioned by the US State Department last month for “knowingly engaging in a significant transaction for the purchase, acquisition, sale, transport or marketing of petrochemical products from Iran.” This has led to speculation that the armed men were unaware of the vessel’s affiliation, and once this was discovered, released it to avoid an entanglement with ally Beijing.



Assessment: Indeed, it is also possible that the SC Taipei had been in distress and was merely being assisted by Iran; however, it has been reported that, prior to its release, the ship was heading toward Bandar Jask, the same location where a Norwegian-owned oil tanker was taken last year after it was hit by an explosion the US blamed on an Iranian mine. Additionally, Tuesday’s episode was reportedly one of several maritime incidents near the Strait of Hormuz recently, as, according to a private shipping firm, a US-flagged container ship was approached by two boats with a raised ladder on March 27, while another tanker said it was approached by IRGC vessels on April 2. While the frequency of harassment and other provocative activities around the Strait of Hormuz has generally tapered off following a spate of such incidents last year, the tensions between the US and Iran that are widely believed to have precipitated those interactions remain escalated, leaving open the possibility that oil tankers, container ships, and other commercial vessels could be targeted as part of Tehran’s efforts to push back against Washington and its Western allies over sanctions burdening its economy. The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations organization has advised vessels operating in the region to exercise vigilance and caution, and to report all suspicious incidents.

Headline: Search Continues for Two Missing Sailors from Cargo Ship that Sank Off of Vietnam
Details:
The Xin Hong, a Panama-flagged cargo ship, sank near Phu Quy Island off the coast of southern Vietnam’s Binh Thuan Province on Thursday afternoon. The ship’s captain had contacted Phu Quy authorities shortly before the incident to request emergency docking permission, but the ship capsized before being able to arrive at the island. There were 11 Chinese and four Vietnamese sailors on board, of whom 11 had been rescued by Friday morning, while two others were found dead. A search for the remaining two crew members was continuing.



Assessment: The Xin Hong was transporting clay from Malaysia to Hong Kong. The accident occurred in rough seas during inclement weather that is believed to have shifted cargo, which caused the ship to list to the side before capsizing. Disruptions to shipping activities are possible in the area while search and rescue operations are carried out for the two outstanding sailors, and there is also the potential for transportation problems arising from loose shipping containers fallen from the ship.

Headline: Traffic restrictions severely disrupt container movements in Mumbai
Details: On August 21, local sources reported that traffic restrictions imposed by the police department in Thane city, a suburb of Mumbai, have severely disrupted export-import container movement at Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust (JNPT) since August 9. The restrictions have been imposed to allow repair works of the Mumbra-Kausa bypass road and a flyover along the road. Container movement to the following terminals are impacted: Gateway Terminals India, Nhava Sheva International Container Terminal (NSICT) and Nhava Sheva (India) Gateway Terminal (NSIGT). The traffic restriction for a few hours on an arterial road linking India’s busiest container port has roiled evacuation of import containers from the port to the container freight stations (CFS) and movement of export boxes to the port, resulting in congestion. As a result, police has stopped traffic movements from and to all terminals from 05:00 to 11:00 and from 17:00 to 23:00 on a daily basis from August 16 for one month, further exacerbating the situation. Trucks will reportedly be stopped at the PUB - Y junction. This week, tractor trailers carrying containers have been stuck on the road for 8-10 hours and inventory has piled up at the terminals.
